tools.name: list_accounts
tools.description: List Drift accounts (the ABM company records), newest batch first

index.description: Starting index for scrolling through accounts (default 0)

tools.name: list_conversations
tools.description: List Drift conversations, optionally narrowed to one status (1 open, 2 closed, 3 pending)

statusId.description: Optional status code to filter by: 1 OPEN, 2 CLOSED, 3 PENDING

page_token.description: Optional pagination token from the previous response's links.next (omit for the first page)

tools.name: get_user
tools.description: Get one Drift user (an internal agent in the org) by numeric user id

needs_review: Tools added 2026-09-12 from the official Drift developer docs (https://devdocs.drift.com/docs/platform-apis): GET /accounts (Listing Accounts), GET /conversations/list (List Conversations) and GET /users/{userId} (Retrieving User). All three are GET reads and carry write:false; contact, conversation and message creation exist in the API and are deliberately out of scope this wave.

THERE IS NO DOCUMENTED /contacts/list ENDPOINT. Drift documents contacts only as GET /contacts/{contactId} (by id) and GET /contacts?email=... (by email, returns a list because email is not a unique identifier). Per the wave brief the contact-list slot therefore falls back to the documented account read, GET /accounts, which is the closest documented list of company records. A contact-by-email read is a fair candidate for a later wave; it is not a list.

THE SCAFFOLDED TEST PATH WAS WRONG AND WAS REPLACED: GET /users/current appears nowhere in the devdocs index (Retrieving User documents GET /users/{userId} and GET /users?userId=, Listing Users documents GET /users/list). The test block is now GET /users/list, which the docs describe as the full list of users in the org with no pagination. Worth recording: a live probe of /users/current also answers 401, so the blind probe alone would NOT have caught the bad path; the documentation did.
AUTH UNCHANGED from the scaffold: the List Conversations page's own curl sample is -H 'Authorization: Bearer <auth_token>', so the scaffolded bearer auth on access_token is what Drift documents.

HOST SPLIT, recorded honestly: the users, contacts and accounts pages document driftapi.com, while the newer List Conversations page documents api.drift.com/conversations/list. Both hosts were probed with a dummy bearer and answered IDENTICALLY (401 {"error":{"message":"The access token is invalid or has expired","type":"authentication_error"}} on documented paths, 404 {"error":{"type":"not_found"}} on the bogus control path), so they front the same edge and base_url stays driftapi.com, which the majority of the docs use. If Salesloft ever retires driftapi.com, this is the single field to change.

SALESLOFT CONSOLIDATION: the vault entry already names this 'Drift (Salesloft)' (acquired 2024). As of 2026-09-12 the Drift developer docs are still served at devdocs.drift.com and both API hosts still answer, but several pages carry 'updated 5 years ago' timestamps and Drift's own product has been folded into Salesloft. Treat this connector as maintenance-risk rather than as a growing surface.

SCOPES: Drift gates these reads per scope (the docs state account_read for the accounts endpoints, and users/conversations have their own). A token missing a scope will surface as a 401/403 from the provider at runtime, not as a spec error.

Shape-proof 2026-09-12 (proofs/drift.proof.json): SHAPE_PROVEN on all 4 probes, each classified on a WWW-Authenticate challenge header (flag www_authenticate) alongside the structured 401 body above; the deterministic control path answered a structurally different 404 not_found. Together that proves host, TLS, the Authorization header name and the routes. No 2xx was ever seen: the field-level response shapes (User, Account and conversation models) come from the documentation, not from this run.
